messages.text: Monday, November 23 · Canton, Michigan
Overcast stillness and the promise of a long-solved riddle

The day brings a quiet, gray chill as we approach the final stretch of November. Local attention turns toward academic discourse in nearby Ann Arbor, while global science grapples with the potential resolution of a centuries-old mathematical mystery.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 49 degrees and a low around 33 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:34 AM and sets at 5:06 PM, with a moon that is full and 97.1 percent illuminated.
Intellectual pursuits in the afternoon

Consider attending the 4 PM seminar at East Hall in Ann Arbor, where Rui Xiong explores a proof of the Grothendieck join-meet positivity. Alternatively, the GalleryDAAS exhibit on women warriors of the African Diaspora opens its doors at 7 PM in Haven Hall.
Mark your calendar for the 862 Meeting taking place on November 25 at 6:30 PM.
Powering the future from home

Ann Arbor's Veridian at County Farm is launching a pilot program as Michigan's first residential virtual power plant. Through this initiative, DTE Energy will manage home batteries to balance grid demand using stored solar energy.
Looking toward the week
Prepare for the 862 Meeting this Tuesday evening to stay informed on local developments.

Tuesday, November 24 · Canton, Michigan
Persian strings, cold iron, and a moon that refuses to wane
The sky holds a full moon above the overcast landscape as we settle into a quiet week. Global sounds in Ann Arbor and local energy policy updates define the current rhythm of our corner of Michigan.
Expect an overcast day with a high of 39 degrees and a low of 24 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:36 AM and sets at 5:05 PM, while the moon remains full and 99.6% illuminated.
Midday music and global sounds
The Stearns Collection Lunchtime Concert Series offers a free performance featuring Persian santour player Alireza Fazel at 12:00 PM in the NCRC Building 18 cafeteria.
A community meeting is scheduled for tomorrow, November 25, at 6:30 PM.
New energy models and research scrutiny

Ann Arbor's Veridian at County Farm is launching a pilot virtual power plant to manage residential solar storage. Meanwhile, a proposed research facility in Ypsilanti Township faces criticism from advocacy groups over its funding and intended use.
